summary: Dana R. in Finance and her entire team cannot access the Finance shared drive (F:), receiving a 'network path not found' error, blocking today's month-end close.
priority_reason: High urgency (hard deadline — month-end close due today) combined with high impact (an entire team is fully blocked with no workaround on a business-critical function), meeting the P1 threshold for a multi-user outage.
clarifying_questions: Roughly what time this morning did the error first appear?
Exactly how many team members are affected, and are they all getting the same 'network path not found' message?
Can you access any other network drives or shared resources (e.g., the internet, email, other mapped drives)?
What is the full server/share path for the F: drive if you know it (e.g., \\server\finance)?
suggested_reply: Hi Dana, thanks for flagging this — I understand how critical it is with month-end close due today, and I've raised it as a P1 given your whole team is blocked. Our Network team is investigating the F: drive 'network path not found' error now. To speed things up, could you confirm what time it started, how many people are affected, and whether other network drives or the internet still work? We'll keep you updated and prioritize restoring access as quickly as possible.
subject: Cannot access shared drive

summary: Production SQL Server 'PRD-SQL-01' has exhausted its connection pool and is rejecting new connections, causing timeouts across multiple customer-facing applications.
priority_reason: High urgency and high impact: a business-critical production database is actively rejecting connections and multiple customer-facing apps are down, affecting many users right now.
suggested_reply: Thanks for the alert. We've raised this as a P1 critical incident and engaged our Database Administration team immediately to investigate the maxed-out connection pool on PRD-SQL-01. They'll work to free or expand connections and restore service to the affected customer-facing apps. We'll post updates as we confirm root cause and recovery. If you have additional telemetry (affected app names, connection counts, or recent deployments), please share it to speed diagnosis.
subject: Database connections maxed out

summary: A coworker encountered a full-screen ransom demand claiming their files are encrypted; they disconnected the network cable.
priority_reason: Active ransomware with encryption in progress is a security breach risking data loss and possible lateral spread to other systems, making it a critical outage regardless of current user count.
clarifying_questions: Who is the affected user and what is their device name/asset tag and physical location?
What is the exact text on the ransom popup (any ransomware family name, payment amount, or deadline)?
Approximately when did the popup first appear?
Is the machine still powered on, and has it been left connected to any docking station, external drives, or shared network storage?
Are any other machines or shared drives showing similar popups or inaccessible files?
suggested_reply: Thank you for reporting this quickly and for unplugging the network cable — that was exactly the right move. Please do NOT power off the machine, pay anything, or click the popup, and leave it disconnected from the network, Wi-Fi, and any external drives. Our Security team is treating this as a critical incident and will contact you immediately. In the meantime, could you tell us the user's name, the device location, and the exact wording on the popup? We're engaging now.
subject: Possible malware popup

summary: Marco received a suspicious email impersonating IT, claiming his mailbox is full and asking him to verify credentials via a link.
priority_reason: Credential-harvesting phishing attempt targeting a user; high urgency as a security threat, though no click or breach confirmed and only one reported user so far — qualifies as at least P2 per security routing rules.
clarifying_questions: Can you forward the suspicious email as an attachment (or share the sender's address and the full link URL) so we can analyze it?
Did you click the link, enter any credentials, or download anything from the email?
Approximately when did you receive it, and have any colleagues reported a similar message?
suggested_reply: Hi Marco, thank you for flagging this and for not clicking the link — that was exactly the right call. This is a classic phishing attempt impersonating IT to steal your password; it is not a legitimate request. Please don't click anything in it. Could you forward the email to us as an attachment so our Security team can investigate and block the sender? If you did happen to click or enter any details, let us know immediately so we can reset your credentials. We'll follow up shortly.
subject: Weird email asking for my password
